Rashi on Eruvin 69b:10:1.hebrew: ביתו אסור להכניס ולהוציא - מביתו לחצר, בין הוא בין שאר בני החצר. ובגמרא מפרש: כשביטל להן רשות שהיה לו בחצר, ולא ביטל להן רשות ביתו. הלכך, הוה ליה רשות ביתו רשות דידיה, וחצר — רשותא דידהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:10:1.english: His house is prohibited to bring in and to take out - From his house into the courtyard, whether [for] him or [for] the rest of the residents of the courtyard. And the Gemara explains: [This is] when he renounced to them the rights that he had in the courtyard, but did not renounce to them the rights to his house. Therefore, the domain of his house is his own domain, and the courtyard is their domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:10:2.hebrew: ושלהם - בתים שלהן מותרין להוציא מהן לחצר, בין הוא בין הן — דהא בתים שלהן וחצר רשות אחת הן:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:10:2.english: And theirs - Their houses are permitted to carry out from them into the courtyard, both for him and for them, for their houses and the courtyard are one domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:10:3.english: They gave him - They [gave him] the rights to their courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:10:4.english: He is permitted - To carry out from his house into the courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:10:5.hebrew: והן אסורין - אפי' מביתו לחצר, ואע"ג דרשות אחת הן. ובגמרא מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:10:5.english: And they are prohibited - Even [to carry] from his house to the courtyard, and even though they are a single domain. And in the Gemara, the reason is explained:

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:11:1.hebrew: היו שנים - ששכחו ולא עירבו, ושאר בני חצר בטלו להן רשותן — שניהן אוסרין זה על זה, מפני שהוא של שניהן, והבתים מיוחדין, כל בית לבעליו, ואין מוציא מרשות המיוחדת לו לרשות שלו ושל חבירו:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:11:1.english: If there were two - Who forgot and did not establish an eiruv, and the other residents of the courtyard renounced their domain to them — both of them prohibit one another, because [the courtyard] belongs to both of them, and the houses are designated, each house to its owner, and one may not carry out from a domain designated to him to a domain belonging to him and his fellow.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:12:1.hebrew: הרי זה אוסר - דמיהדר ומשקל רשותא הוא, וחזר בו מביטולו:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:12:1.english: He renders [carrying] prohibited - For he is going back and taking [back his] rights, and has retracted his renunciation.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:13:1.hebrew: הא חצירו - רשות שהיתה לו בחצירו שריא לבני החצר, ומותר להן להוציא מבתיהן לחצר, כדקתני מתניתין להדיא:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:13:1.english: His courtyard, however, [is permitted] - The domain rights that he had in his courtyard are permitted to the residents of the courtyard, and it is permitted for them to carry out from their houses into the courtyard, as the Mishnah teaches explicitly.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:14:1.english: If he renounced - His rights to the residents of the courtyard:

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:14:2.english: Why is his house prohibited - Behold, he gave them his house and withdrew.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:14:3.hebrew: ואי דלא בטיל - מידי, רשות חצירו מאן שרייה:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:14:3.english: And if he did not renounce - Anything — who permitted the domain of his courtyard?

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:14:4.hebrew: וקסברי רבנן - תנא דמתני', דסתמא היא, ופליגא אדר' אליעזר, דאמר בפרק עושין פסין (לעיל עירובין דף כו:): ביתו אסור להכניס ולהוציא לו, אבל להם מותר — דהמבטל רשות חצירו, רשות ביתו ביטל:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:14:4.english: And the Rabbis hold - [This refers to] the Tanna of our Mishnah, as it is an anonymous [Mishnah]; and it disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer, who said in the chapter [entitled] Osin Passin (above, Eruvin 26b): [With regard to] his house, it is prohibited to bring in and to take out for him, but for them it is permitted, as one who renounces the rights to his courtyard renounces the rights to his house.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:15:1.hebrew: דהוי אורח לגבייהו - כיון דמביתו לא מפיק, אע"ג דמשתמש בחצר — לא מיהדר ומשקל רשותיה הוא, אלא כשאר אורחין:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:15:1.english: For he is like a guest to them - Since he does not carry out from his [own] house, even though he uses the courtyard, he is not returning and taking back his domain, but rather [is] like other guests.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:16:1.hebrew: והן אסורין - אפי' מביתו לחצר — דכיון דמשתמשי בחצר, אע"ג דלאו מבית דידהו מפקי, הוה ליה משקל רשותא, דחמשה לגבי חד לא דמו לאורחין:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:16:1.english: And they are prohibited - Even from his house to the courtyard — for since they make use of the courtyard, even though they do not take [items] out from their [own] houses, it constitutes reclaiming [their] domain, as five vis-à-vis one are not considered like guests.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:17:1.hebrew: שמע מינה מבטלין כו' - דמשמע נתנו לו רשות ארישא קאי, דקתני ושלהן מותר לו ולהן, דבטל להם רשותו; חזרו הם ונתנו לו רשותן — הוא מותר:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:17:1.english: Learn from this [that] one may renounce, etc. - For it implies that [the clause], "They gave him [their] rights," refers to the opening clause [of the mishna], which taught: "And theirs is permitted to him and to them," where he [had] renounced his rights to them; [and then] they in turn gave him their rights — [so] he is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:19:1.hebrew: היו שנים - ששכחו ולא עירבו עם השאר, ובטלו להן חבריהן רשותן — אוסרין שניהן זה על זה:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:19:1.english: If there were two - Who forgot and did not establish an eiruv with the rest, and their companions renounced their rights to them — both of them prohibit one another.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:19:2.hebrew: פשיטא - דאי הוו תרוייהו לחודייהו מעיקרא, הוו אסרי אהדדי:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:19:2.english: [Isn't this] obvious? - For had the two of them been by themselves from the outset, they would have prohibited one another.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:19:3.english: No, [it is] necessary where one went back and renounced to his fellow - [He renounced] his own domain and his share in the domain that their fellows had renounced to them.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:19:4.hebrew: מהו דתימא לישתרו - דהוו להו כחמשה ששרויין בחצר ולא עירבו, דמבטלי רשותא לחד מינייהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:19:4.english: Lest you say let them be permitted - For they would be like five [people] who dwell in a courtyard and did not establish an eiruv, who renounce [their] rights to one of them.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:19:5.hebrew: קמ"ל - דלא דמי: דאילו התם, כל חד וחד מבטל ליה רשותיה; אבל הכא, כיון דשאר בני חצר לאו להאי דפייש לחודיה בטלי, אלא לתרוייהו — כי הדר חד ומבטל לאידך, רשותא דידיה מצי לבטולי, רשותא דאקני ליה חבריה לא מצי לבטולי. דכיון דבעידנא דבטלי להו הנך קמאי רשותייהו, אפ"ה לא הוה להאי מבטל שריותא בהאי חצר, משום דאסרי אהדדי — אשתכח דבטול דקמאי לא אהני; וכי הדר מבטל האי, לא מצי לאקנויי רשותא דידהו, דהא לא קנייה:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:19:5.english: [The mishna] teaches us - That it is not comparable: For there, each and every one renounced his domain to him; but here, since the other residents of the courtyard did not renounce [their domain] to this [resident] who remains alone, but rather to both of them, when one [of them] turns around and renounces [his rights] to the other — his own domain he can renounce, [but] the domain that his fellow [residents] transferred to him he cannot renounce. For since at the time when those initial [residents] renounced their domain to them, this renouncer nevertheless had no permission [to carry] in this courtyard, because they prohibited one another — it turns out that the renunciation of the initial [residents] was of no effect; and when this one turns around and renounces [his rights], he cannot transfer their domain, for he did not acquire it.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:1:1.hebrew: עד דהוי מומר לע"ג - דההוא ודאי חשוד לכל מילי, דאמר מר: חמורה ע"ג, שכל המודה בה ככופר בכל התורה כולה, דכתיב: "וכי תשגו ולא תעשו את כל המצות האלה", ובע"ג משתעי קרא, בהוריות (דף ח.):
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:1:1.english: Unless he is an apostate with regard to idolatry - For that one is certainly suspected with regard to all matters [of the Torah], as the Master said: "Idolatry is [so] severe that anyone who acknowledges it is like one who denies the entire Torah," as it is written: "And when you shall err, and not observe all these commandments" — and the verse speaks of idolatry, [as explained] in Horayot (8a).

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:20:1.hebrew: נותן תנינא - ושלהם מותר לו ולהן, ואי לאו דבטיל ליה — אמאי משתרו:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:20:1.english: Giving, we learned [it] - "And theirs is permitted to him and to them" — and were it not that he renounced [his rights] to them, why would they be permitted?

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:20:2.hebrew: נוטל תנינא - נתנו לו, אלמא יחיד נוטל רשות:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:20:2.english: Receiving, we learned [it] - [From the words,] "They gave to him" — evidently an individual receives rights.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:2:1.hebrew: אמר רב נחמן - איזהו ישראל מומר דקאמר רב הונא לעיל, לענין ביטול רשות קאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:2:1.english: Rav Naḥman said - That which Rav Huna said above, "Who is an apostate Jew?", he said with regard to renouncing [domain] rights.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:2:2.hebrew: בשוק - בפרהסיא, ואע"ג דמחלל בצנעא:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:2:2.english: In the marketplace - In public, even though he desecrates [it] in private.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:3:1.english: How so? - [This] refers to [the case of] an Israelite.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:3:2.english: “May my rights be acquired by you” - Or, “May my rights be renounced to you.”

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:3:3.english: To take possession - Through an acquisition with a scarf.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:4:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - לעולם מומר דקאמר רב הונא, לכל מילי קחשיב ליה מומר, וכרבנן ס"ל, והאי תנא הוא דאלימא ליה שבת כע"ג:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:4:1.english: Rav Ashi said - Actually, when Rav Huna said “an apostate,” he considered him an apostate with regard to all matters, and he holds in accordance with the Rabbis; and it is this Tanna for whom Shabbat is as severe as idolatry:

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:5:1.hebrew: אדם כי יקריב מכם פרט למומר - דאין מקבלין קרבנות, דמכם משמע מקצתכם:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:5:1.english: “When any man of you brings an offering” — to the exclusion of an apostate - That offerings are not accepted [from him], as “of you” implies some of you.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:5:2.hebrew: מכם - מדכתיב האי מיעוטא גבי ישראל, ולא כתיב "כי יקריב מן האדם קרבן", ש"מ: בישראל הוא דחלק ומיעט מומר:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:5:2.english: “Of you” - Since this exclusion is written regarding Israel, and it is not written: “When [a person] brings an offering from mankind,” learn from this that it is among Israel that He made a distinction and excluded an apostate.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:5:3.hebrew: ולא באומות - שמקבלין קרבן מכולם, כדתניא: ״איש״ — מה ת"ל ״איש איש״? לרבות את הנכרים, שנודרין נדרים ונדבות כישראל, בהכל שוחטין (חולין דף יג:):
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:5:3.english: And not among the nations - For an offering is accepted from all of them, as it is taught: “[Since the verse says] ‘a man’ — why does the verse state: ‘Any man’ [ish ish]? To include gentiles, who [may] vow vow-offerings and gift-offerings like an Israelite” — in [the chapter entitled] Hakol Shochatin (Chullin 13b).

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:6:1.hebrew: להביא בני אדם הדומין לבהמה - רשעים שעשו עצמן כבהמה שאינה מכרת את בוראה, מקבלין מהן קרבן:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:6:1.english: To include people who are similar to animals - Wicked people who made themselves like an animal that does not recognize its Creator — we accept a sacrifice from them.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:6:2.hebrew: מקבלין קרבנות - של נדבה מפושעי ישראל, דהאי קרא בנדרים ונדבות משתעי, דכתיב: ״כי יקריב״:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:6:2.english: We accept sacrifices - [Meaning,] voluntary [offerings] from Jewish transgressors, for this verse speaks of vows and voluntary offerings, as it is written: “When [any man of you] brings [an offering].”

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:6:3.hebrew: כדי שיחזרו בתשובה - דאי דחינן להו בידים, תו לא הדרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:6:3.english: In order that they repent - For if we push them away with [our own] hands, they will not return anymore.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:8:1.english: And one who pours the wine - For idol worship.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:9:1.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it is saying - We accept sacrifices from Jewish transgressors who are apostates with regard to one matter.

Rashi on Eruvin 69b:9:2.hebrew: חוץ מן המומר לנסך את היין או לחלל שבת - דכמומר לכל התורה דמי, דאימעיט ליה: "מכם" — ולא כולכם:
Rashi on Eruvin 69b:9:2.english: Except for an apostate with regard to pouring wine [libations] or desecrating Shabbat - For he is considered like an apostate with regard to the entire Torah, who is excluded [by the verse]: "Of you" — and not all of you.

Tosafot on Eruvin 69b:15:1.hebrew: ושלהם מותר לו ולהן - "דהוי אורח לגבייהו", פירש ר"ח: דאמר בירושלמי, "אכסנאי אינו אוסר לעולם". ואומר ר"י דלא דמי להכא כלל, דהתם איירי כגון הבא לדור במבוי לשם אכסנאות ולא לקבוע עצמו, דהכי איתא התם: אית תנא תני, "קסדור אוסר מיד ואכסנאי לאחר שלשים", ואית תנא תני, "קסדור אוסר לאחר שלשים ואכסנאי אינו אוסר לעולם". מ"ד "קסדור אוסר מיד" — ברגיל, "ואכסנאי לאחר שלשים" — בשאינו רגיל; מ"ד "קסדור לאחר שלשים" — כאלין דעלין ברשות, "ואכסנאי אינו אוסר לעולם" — כאלין דלא עלין ברשות:
Tosafot on Eruvin 69b:15:1.english: "And their [houses] are permitted to him and to them" - [Regarding the statement,] "For he is a guest of theirs": Rabbeinu Chananel explained that it says in the Yerushalmi: "A guest never prohibits." But the Ri says that this is not comparable to here at all, for there it is dealing with, for example, one who comes to reside in an alleyway for the purpose of [temporary] lodging and not to establish himself [permanently]. For so it is stated there: One Tanna teaches: "An officer [kasdor] prohibits immediately, and a guest [akhsanai] after thirty [days]"; and one Tanna teaches: "An officer prohibits after thirty [days], and a guest never prohibits." The one who says "an officer prohibits immediately" [holds that it applies to one who is] a regular [visitor], and "a guest after thirty" — when he is not a regular [visitor]; the one who says "an officer after thirty" — [is referring to] those who enter with permission, and "a guest never prohibits" — [is referring to] those who do not enter with permission.
